sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for OCR settings
sections.what: Loads the settings library and its base class, and adds a one-line description of the file.
sections.why: Needed to read settings from the environment and files.
sections.watch_out: If the library is missing, the service stops at import time.

sections.name: Settings
sections.title: Settings and their defaults
sections.what: Defines the OCR settings: environment, log level, queue address, storage endpoint and login, bucket, optional Google key, and language codes, each with a default.
sections.why: Likely reason: defaults let local development run without setup. Reason for these particular values is not stated.
sections.watch_out: The default storage login is a known local value and must not be used in a shared environment.

summary: Loads the OCR service settings from environment variables and a local .env file, with defaults for each one.
purpose: Gives the OCR service one place for queue, storage, Google key, and language settings.
why: Likely reason: keeps secrets out of the code. Reason for the chosen defaults is not stated.
how: Defines each setting with a default: environment, log level, queue address, storage endpoint, access key, secret key, bucket, optional Google key, and language codes. Reads values from the environment and a .env file in the current folder, ignores unknown names, and creates one shared settings object.
inputs: Environment variables and a .env file in the folder the program starts from.
outputs: A shared settings object used by the OCR code.
risks: The .env file is found relative to the folder the program starts from, so starting from another folder silently ignores it. The storage defaults are well known. A blank Google key quietly turns the fallback off.
debug: If settings look like the defaults, check the starting folder and the environment variables. Confirm the storage endpoint and bucket match the running storage server.
